title: Sitting in at the Maison Bourbon
summary: Riddick tells of sitting in the previous Sunday with Milton Rich's band, singing Black and Blue.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, when you used to go sit in, you know, just for fun, you didn't drink then, did you?

Yeah. Where would you go to sit in? Who would you like to sit in? Just where you happened to be. Well, last Sunday night, I passed by the Maison Bourbon, but of course I was not drinking at all. And I never had a drink that night, for that matter. But it was Milton Rich's band. And they asked me, the piano player, said I heard her name, Alan something.
I can't think of his name. Very fine piano man.

He said, I heard so much about you. He said, I'd love to hear you play. I said, well, I don't play like you. I play like me. He says, that's why I want to hear you, because I heard so many fine things about the way the solid piano player that you are. So Dick Johnson asked me, does he play? So he says, come on and sit in and play a couple of tunes. So I played three tunes and sang black and blue. And they seemed to be very happy with it. Sidney Snow was playing bass. Oscar, what's your name, on tenor sax and baritone sax and clarinet.
